title: Long-horizon support lanes: mapping, rollback policies, and upgrade automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, our customers need predictable, long-lived stability guarantees across four product surfaces (serving runtime, public API, SDKs, Console). Current ad-hoc versioning produces confusion during upgrades: SDKs drift, console expects different API shapes, and runtime ABI/kv-cache behavior changes create silent regressions.

Proposal summary: Define a set of durable support lanes (names, SLAs, and timelines), a consumable cross-surface compatibility matrix, and an automated gating and rollback pipeline that enforces compatibility and minimizes customer disruption. The proposal covers: 1) Support lane taxonomy, 2) Compatibility guarantees per surface, 3) Rollout gates and monitoring thresholds, 4) Upgrade automation (preflight checks, staged rollout orchestration, automated rollback), 5) Documentation and deprecation timelines.

Support lanes (draft):
- Durable (DUR): long-horizon LTS for customers needing multi-year stability; ABI and API compatibility guaranteed within a major; security/critical patches backported.
- Maintenance (MNT): 9-18 month supported lane with security and selected bug fixes.
- Rolling (MAIN): default dev lane with frequent feature releases and no long-term backports.

Cross-surface compatibility guarantees (high-level):
- Runtime: preserve model-serving ABI and cache semantics for DUR lanes; breaking optimizations must be feature-flagged and opt-in.
- API: maintain request/response contract and structured output stability for DUR; introduce V+X minor additions only via additive fields and version negotiation.
- SDKs: semver mapping so SDK major matches API/runtime major when surface-breaking changes are required; provide polyfilled shims for minor mismatches for one release window.
- Console: UI/UX expects stable route and schema shapes for DUR; console feature flags must be available to handle newer API fields without breaking older clusters.

Rollout gates and metrics (examples):
- Canary window: 1% traffic for 24h with absolute error rate delta <0.05% and p95 latency delta <10ms.
- Quality gate: regressions in eval benchmark suites (prompt set) must be <= 0.5% failures vs baseline.
- Cost gate: average token cost delta <= 3% for REQUEST_TYPE=embedding or generation.
- Stability gate: no crash loops or memory-growth signals beyond threshold on dedicated pools.

Automation and tooling:
- preflight: automated compatibility matrix generator that queries SDK/API/runtime version contracts and runs an integration matrix in CI (cross-version smoke tests + evals).
- rollout orchestrator: pipeline that sequences deploys across surfaces, verifies gates, and can automatically rollback to the last green version.
- migration helper: autogenerated SDK and Console migration guidance (diffs of API schemas, example client patches).
- observability: dashboard template (Console) and alert set that maps gate failures to owner teams and provides one-click rollback.

Documentation and deprecation:
- A public support matrix hosted in the docs site and mirrored to an internal canonical JSON in the repo.
- Deprecation calendar: 6 months notice for removals in Maintenance lanes, 12 months for Durable majors.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increased maintenance cost for Durable lanes (backports, test-matrix growth).
- Slower shipping cadence for features that must remain compatible.
- Tooling complexity required to keep rollout automation safe across private deployments.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Finalize lane SLAs with Product/Sales by 2026-03-19.
2) Implement canonical compatibility JSON schema and generator (ENG task) by 2026-04-02.
3) Build CI cross-version smoke tests and integrate into release pipeline (estimate 4 sprints).
4) Prototype rollout orchestrator runbook for staging and run a full dry-run (runtime/API/SDK/Console) by 2026-04-30.

Long-term goal: ship a single-release playbook that teams can adopt to certify a release against the compatibility matrix and allow customers to opt into Durable lanes with clear SLAs and rollback guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical support matrix JSON exists in repo and is published to internal docs site
Compatibility generator runs in CI and emits cross-surface matrix for every PR that touches runtime/API/SDK/Console
Release pipeline enforces canary and quality gates; failures block rollout and notify owners
Rollback automation tested in staging with a documented runbook and run against a simulated production incident
SDKs have a published semver mapping doc and example migration patches for at least two common languages
PM and Security have signed off on lane definitions and deprecation timelines
